name: Polycab India Ltd
about: Polycab is India’s leading manufacturers of cables and wires and allied products such as uPVC conduits and lugs and glands. We have a range of cables and wires for practically every application. More recently Polycab has also launched a wide range of consumer electrical products like Fans, Switches, Switchgear, LED lights and Luminaries, Solar Inverters, and Pumps.

sections.one_liner: India's largest wires and cables maker. The question now is whether record margins and 11-day working capital last.
business: Wires and cables are 87% of revenue, with a 30-31% share of the organised market, up from 26-27% a year earlier [AR FY26][Q4FY26 call]
Consumer electrical goods (FMEG) are 7% of revenue and turned profitable. EPC (power projects) is 6%, with a ₹11,300 cr order book and 9.9% margins [AR FY26]
Exports were ₹1,570 cr, or 5.4% of revenue, across 94 countries. Management targets more than 10% by FY30 [AR FY26][Q1FY27 call]
Revenue comes mostly from domestic retail channels plus institutional and project sales. Copper, aluminium and PVC are the main input costs [AR FY26]
financial_snapshot: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): revenue ₹9,899 cr, up 52.8% YoY; EBITDA ₹1,422 cr at 14.4%; PAT ₹990 cr, up 42.9% YoY [Numbers]
Last four quarters: revenue ₹34,609 cr, EBITDA ₹4,685 cr (13.5% margin), PAT ₹3,203 cr. PAT is growing about 10 points slower than revenue [Numbers]
ROCE is 33.2% but ROE only 23.0%. ₹4,520 cr of net cash, about 35% of net worth, holds equity returns down [Numbers][Q2FY27 call]
Market cap ₹1,17,355 cr; P/E 37.2x (36.6x on last-four-quarter PAT); 9.0x book; 0.6% dividend yield; price 23% below its ₹10,129 high [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue grew from ₹8,792 cr to ₹28,884 cr between FY21 and FY26: 26.9% a year over 5 years, 27.0% over 3 [Numbers]
EBITDA grew about 29% a year over 5 years, but PAT only 25.0%. PAT fell from 80% to 67% of EBITDA [Numbers]
Operating margin is stuck in a 10-14% range. FY26's 14.0% is only 0.7 points above the prior 3-year average [Numbers]
ROCE rose from 23% in FY21 to 33% in FY26. Quarterly margin went 16% (Sep 2025), then 13%, 13%, now 14%: input-cost swings show through quickly [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings are ₹272 cr against ₹13,094 cr net worth (debt/equity 0.02). Net cash rose from ₹2,940 cr to ₹4,520 cr in a year [Numbers][Q2FY27 call]
Working capital days fell from 54 to 30 in FY26 and to 11 by Q2 FY27. Management calls 11 days abnormal and guides 45-50 [Numbers][Q2FY27 call]
Debtor days (42 to 48) and inventory days (86 to 99) both rose. My estimate is payable days went from about 64 to 108, so suppliers are funding the business [Numbers]
cash_quality: Operating cash flow was 1.05x PAT over 3 years but 1.41x in FY26 (₹3,811 cr vs ₹2,708 cr), lifted by working-capital release [Numbers]
Free cash flow went ₹969 cr, ₹438 cr, ₹853 cr, then ₹2,340 cr. FY26 is an outlier driven by working capital, not a new run-rate [Numbers]
Getting back to 45-50 days from 11 means about 35 days of revenue, roughly ₹3,300 cr, flowing back out. That is close to FY26 free cash flow [Numbers][Q2FY27 call]
narrative_vs_numbers: Revenue grew 53% but wires and cables volumes grew only mid-to-high single digits. Roughly 40+ points is price, so earnings follow copper, not demand [Q2FY27 call][Numbers]
Wires and cables margin of 14.4% is above management's own 11-13% long-term range. Management says it will normalise, which means it expects margins to fall [Q2FY27 call]
Q4 FY26 shows the risk: revenue up 26.9% but PAT up only 7.1%. Price hikes of 18-19% lagged input costs [Numbers][Q4FY26 call]
The share-gain story fits the numbers: 29% revenue growth in FY26 against an 11-12% market, and 18% volume growth [Q4FY26 call][Numbers]
guidance: Wires and cables EBITDA margin: 12-14% near-to-mid term, 11-13% long term; repeated on the Q2 FY27 call [Q4FY26 call][Q2FY27 call]
Wires and cables volume: 1.5x market growth. Market at 12-13% implies 18-20% for Polycab [Q2FY27 call]
FMEG: grow 1.5-2x the industry, with 8-10% EBITDA margin by FY30 [Q1FY27 call][Q2FY27 call]
Capex ₹6,000-8,000 cr over 5 years (₹1,200-1,600 cr a year), funded internally. Dividend payout above 30% by FY30, from 27.2% [Q4FY26 call]
Working capital back to 45-50 days. EPC margin in the high single digits. EHV plant now FY28 [Q2FY27 call]

ledger.promised: Wires and cables EBITDA 12-14% near-to-mid term [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Group margin 13.8% in Q1, 14.4% in Q2; wires and cables cited at 14.4%, at the top of range

ledger.promised: Capex ₹1,200-1,600 cr a year under Project Spring [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: ₹1,480 cr in FY26 (cash flow less free cash flow ₹1,471 cr); ₹610 cr in H1 FY27

ledger.promised: Solar momentum to continue in coming quarters [Q3FY26 call]

ledger.promised: EHV capacity online by end of calendar 2026 [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Five months later, pushed to 'somewhere in FY2028' [Q2FY27 call]

ledger.promised: EPC margin in the high single digits [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: EPC margin 7.2% in Q2 on ₹617 cr revenue, below FY26's 9.9%

ledger.promised: FMEG EBITDA margin 8-10% by FY30 [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: FMEG operating margin 10.1% in Q2 FY27, already at the top of target

bull: FMEG grew 124% with a 10.1% operating margin, three years ahead of target. A second profit engine beyond the 87% wires and cables base [Q2FY27 call]
₹4,520 cr net cash covers about 3 years of ₹1,200-1,600 cr capex. ROCE of 33% with no debt [Numbers][Q4FY26 call]
Organised-market share rose about 4 points to 30-31%. Revenue compounded 27% a year over 3 years with margins at 13-14% [AR FY26][Numbers]
bear: Management itself guides wires and cables margins down 1.4-3.4 points from 14.4% to 11-13%. At 37x P/E, the price assumes today's margins hold [Q2FY27 call][Numbers]
Working capital going from 11 to 45-50 days would pull about ₹3,300 cr back out. Single-digit volumes mean copper prices are carrying revenue growth [Numbers][Q2FY27 call]
UltraTech is entering wires at a 10-15% discount. EHV slipped about a year. Q3 FY27 faces a 46% growth base [Q2FY27 call][Numbers]
questions: How much of Q2's 53% growth is volume, how much copper price?
Payable days roughly 108: how much supplier credit reverses when copper falls?
Why did EHV slip from December 2026 to FY28? Any cost overrun?
What wires and cables margin do you assume if UltraTech's discount spreads?

annual_report.business: India's No.1 wires and cables manufacturer serving industrial, retail and institutional customers. Also operates FMEG (consumer electrical goods) and EPC (power infrastructure projects). Makes money through product sales across domestic and export markets with backward integration.

segments.name: Cables and Wires
segments.comment: Market leader, 30-31% organized share, strong domestic/export

segments.name: Fast-Moving Electrical Goods
segments.comment: 25% YoY growth, turned profitable; consumer electronics

annual_report.revenue_mix: Domestic cables/wires dominant; exports to 90+ countries (₹15.7Bn, 5.4%); institutional and project-based complement retail distribution
strategy: Project Spring: Five-year transformation to FY2029-30 for growth
Digital DNA: AI and loyalty apps for retail engagement
Expand W&C organized market share consolidation domestically
FMEG expansion targeting top 3 in key segments
Build international presence via supply chain diversification
annual_report.outlook: Strong growth momentum expected, anchored by W&C market leadership. Supported by infrastructure investments, power sector growth, renewable energy, real estate upcycle, and electrification. Positioned to consolidate domestic market leadership.

Commodity price volatility (copper, aluminium, PVC, steel)
Geopolitical tensions affecting Middle East operations and shipping
